title: TransportEnvelope
description: The four WebSocket frame shapes exchanged between the laptop (server) and the phone (client); see docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 4.2 and Sec 4.4 and contracts/README.md 'Transport envelope'. The reserved type 'location' (phone -> laptop, defined in a later step) and any other unrecognised 'type' are valid JSON that a receiver logs and ignores -- they are deliberately out of scope for this schema, which only documents the shapes the laptop and phone actually exchange today.

t1.description: Laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.
Echoed laptop send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t2.description: Phone receive time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

t3.description: Phone send time, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds.

health.description: Phone -> laptop. One report of the feedback manager's stale-drop ring (10 one-second buckets of {received, staleDropped}); a rising rate is the trigger for the docs/camera-sync-design.md Sec 3.4 automatic fallback. Advisory only: the laptop's health monitor still steps rungs and flips to the local detector without it, and a report older than 3 s (after clock conversion) is ignored, so a dead signal can never drive a switch.

t_phone_ms.description: When the phone produced this report, integer Unix-epoch milliseconds in the PHONE clock (the laptop converts before judging freshness).

window_ms.description: Width of the whole ring in milliseconds (10 one-second buckets = 10000).

received.description: Events the feedback manager received inside the window.

stale_dropped.description: Of those, the ones dropped for arriving past their TTL (Sec 4.4).

stale_drop_rate.description: stale_dropped / received over the complete buckets; 0 when received is 0. At or above 0.2 over at least 2 complete buckets the laptop flips to the local detector.

complete_buckets.description: How many of the ring's one-second buckets are fully elapsed. Fewer than 2 makes the rate meaningless, and the laptop ignores the report.
